item.text:
**3B.3 Research Note: Fumio Kishida (2024)**

**Assessment:** I found no credible 2024 evidence that Kishida personally incited hatred, revenge, dehumanization, scapegoating, or violence against minorities, migrants, journalists, civil society, or other protected groups. The record is strongly negative on incitement: Kishida repeatedly used inclusive, anti-discrimination, and human-rights language. The closest mixed signal is not incitement itself but a harder migration/security policy frame on “illegal foreigners,” which is policy-coded rather than hate-coded.

- [Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** February 5, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida said Japan must not tolerate unfair discrimination or violence against foreigners, Ainu people, sexual minorities, or other minorities; he explicitly invoked the rule of law, fundamental human rights, and human dignity and said the government would stand firm against prejudice.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.3, 3B.1

- [National Statement (Commitment) Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida on the Occasion of the Third Summit for Democracy](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/20message.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** March 20, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida framed human rights, business-and-human-rights standards, women’s empowerment, and child rights as pillars of a peaceful, stable society, with no scapegoating language toward opponents or marginalized groups.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.3, 3B.2

- [Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida on International Women’s Day](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/08message2.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** March 8, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida emphasized women’s empowerment, gender equality, and combating sexual violence and sexual crime, while pledging support for survivors and victims. This is affirmative anti-abuse rhetoric, not dehumanization or incitement.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.3, 3B.2, 3B.1

- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida Regarding the Messages of Life Exhibition](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/15kaiken.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** May 15, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida said protecting lives from crime and traffic accidents is a core government role and described steps to review dangerous-driving laws and support victims’ families. This is victim-centered public safety language, not hate speech or revenge incitement.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.3, 3B.2

- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida Regarding the Ruling on a Lawsuit over the Former Eugenics Protection Law and Other Matters](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** July 3, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida called forced sterilization an unacceptable infringement of human rights, offered profound apology, and said the government would compensate victims and ensure it never happens again. This is direct repudiation of state-led dehumanization.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.3, 3B.2, 3B.1

- [AP coverage of Kishida’s migration / “illegal foreigners zero” framing on his official site](https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/)  
  - **Publisher:** Kishida Fumio official website / Liberal Democratic Party-affiliated site  
  - **Date:** 2024 page content  
  - **Claim-level summary:** The page presents a tougher “illegal foreigners zero” agenda, including visa screening, deportation/enforcement, and tighter refugee procedures. This is the closest mixed signal I found, but it is policy-oriented border enforcement rather than personal incitement against foreigners or migrants.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.3

**Search gap:** I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Kishida personally encouraged hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against opponents, minorities, migrants, journalists, civil society, or ethnic/religious groups. The available record points the other way: inclusive-society and human-rights messaging, plus explicit rejection of discrimination and violence.
